en: Mayon Volcano in Albay province is famous for having a nearly perfect conical shape created by layers of hardened lava.
The Philippine tarsier, native to Bohol, possesses enormous eyes that are actually larger in size than its entire brain.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley in Luzon.
Lake Lanao in Mindanao is the largest lake in the island and the second-largest lake in the entire Philippines.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features a navigable cave river that flows directly out into the West Philippine Sea.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a strictly protected marine sanctuary containing hundreds of coral species.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains by indigenous people over 2,000 years ago.
The amihan is the cool northeast monsoon wind that brings dry weather to the Philippines from November to February.
The Philippines is a top global producer of nickel ore, which is primarily mined in the Surigao region of Mindanao.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, is endemic to Mindanao and Luzon forests and features a distinctive crest of long feathers.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry summer season.
